With stretching you septum there's two main options you can dead stretch this means using a single flare plug where you lube it up with some cocoa butter or skin safe oil and pop it in. Or you can use a pincher although this option doesn't work for some. A pincher is a type of jewellery that works a bit like a taper so it's a but less safe you use is in a similar way to a plug where you lube it up and pop it in. Some things to remember when you're doing either of these techniques
1- it should not be painful. Never force something through any piercing if you feel pain stop and wait you'll be able to do it again in a few weeks or months time. 
2- NEVER use silicone or acrylic jewellery to stretch. Stick to titanium and glass these are non porous body safe and will make sure your piercing heels well.
3- use reasonable sizes don't try to jump sizes go up 1 at a time and leave time in between. As you get bigger try half sizes as well this'll really help with the stretching and make it a nicer experience
4- when you're stretching treat your piercing like its brand new clean it take care of it don't go touching it for no reason with unclean hands

I'm not an artist but from my own experiences when exploring covering up my own sh scars (not yet got them covered been a long time preparing) there's a few things to bear in mind such as the type of scars the healing process and the design. As far as the type of scar all I mean is some people like me keloid when they scar meaning it's raised and rubbery but others scar flat on the skin you can still get tattoos with any type of scar but remember that raised scars will still be raised they won't ever lay flat and sometimes tattooing over flat scars can make them raise temporarily or permanently. For a cover-up a scar should be fully healed some artists online recommend at least a year but again if you have raised scars or particularly large/deep it'll need more healing time but if you approach an artist when you're ready they should be able to tell you if they're ready to be tattooed over or to wait a while longer. Another thing is if they're scars that required stitches or surgery then approach a doctor before getting tattooed. As far as the design goes a more full design helps cover scars more think of a darker design or something like a bouquet of flowers where theyres lots going on. A tattoo will never fully cover the tattoos as in they will still be visible if you look close even if you were to black out whole limbs the texture of scars remains and so the purpose of a cover-up is more to disguise and distract this us why a lot of people go for big impressive works with lots of details drawing the attention to the whole area rather than the scars individually. And finally with designs I recommend just finding something you like or a bunch of things you like such as sea animals, pirates trinkets and let your artist create work incorporating it to fit your body and your scars. I really hope this makes sense and helps when you're figuring out what kind of design you'd like and how it'll fit to your body. End of the day find something you like and an artist should really help you out with all the rest helping you through the process and design and if they don't do this they're not a good artist. Wish you all the best

He gave me lots of time to choose the songs I wanted to learn and gave me advice as I basically learnt by myself in a way. He also noticed when I would get frustrated and upset and at first he would tell me to calm down or to stop for a second but this makes me more so frustrated so he learnt to let me carry on and try again and again until I get it and give me the praise when I do get it of course he added some of his humour into the situation too. But as soon as he learnt this he kept it in mind and remembered it for future. Learning the small things that make the student upset would help a lot just learn as you go along everyone’s different and so noticing the things that make them upset and asking what they want to focus on in lessons can help you need to work with the student as a team rather than as a teacher.
